title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-005: Is per-deposit-event CPU cost in extract_deposit_data bounded to prevent DoS?
skip_reason: Component mismatch: extract_deposit_data CPU cost in EL context, Prysm is CL

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: Analysis skipped due to component mismatch. The property PROP-W6B15-34 concerns the extract_deposit_data function, which is part of the Execution Layer (EL) block processing pipeline. Prysm is a Consensus Layer (CL) client and does not implement EL-specific deposit extraction logic. The specified code scope targets execution-layer components, but Prysm operates at the consensus layer where deposit data is received already processed from the EL client via the Engine API.

component_analysis.explanation: The extract_deposit_data function is responsible for parsing and validating deposit events from the deposit contract during EL block processing. This function exists in EL clients (like Geth, Nethermind, Besu, Erigon) but not in CL clients (like Prysm, Lighthouse, Teku, Nimbus). CL clients receive deposit data through the Engine API after EL processing has already occurred.

el_responsibility: Process deposit contract logs from executed blocks
Extract and validate deposit event data
Forward validated deposits to CL via Engine API
cl_responsibility: Receive deposit data from EL via Engine API
architectural_context.trust_boundary: tb-005 (P2P to State) applies at EL layer for this property, not CL layer

abstract_interpretation_n_a.reason: No applicable code scope in consensus layer client

phase1_abstract_interpretation.recommendation: This check should be applied to Execution Layer clients (Geth, Nethermind, Besu, Erigon) rather than Consensus Layer client Prysm. For proper audit coverage, re-scope this check to target EL implementations where extract_deposit_data is actually implemented.

suggested_focus: CPU cost bounds for deposit signature verification in CL
Resource limits for processing deposit messages received via Engine API
DoS protection for maximum deposits per block at CL processing stage
Validation efficiency for deposit data already extracted by EL
